traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb Zingiberales page (read 2026-10-16): Strelitziaceae and Heliconiaceae two-ranked, Musaceae and Cannaceae spiral; Wikipedia Zingiberaceae and Marantaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves in two rows. 'Usually' by Zingiberaceae and Marantaceae weight.

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): blades entire with a midrib and S-shaped lateral veins (tearing in bananas does not make leaflets).

traits.life_span.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): large rhizomatous herbs, rarely trees; Wikipedia Zingiberaceae (read 2026-10-16): perennial herbs with creeping rhizomes.

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Zingiberaceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers in racemes with spirally set bracts; Wikipedia Marantaceae: spike or panicle; Wikipedia Costaceae: a terminal spike. Our weighting follows Zingiberaceae (largest family).

traits.flowering_position.note: Wikipedia Costaceae (read 2026-10-16): terminal spike in most genera; APweb (read 2026-10-16): Lowiaceae flowers axillary. Gingers bear the inflorescence either at the tip of the leafy shoot or on a separate shoot from the rhizome; we read both as terminal (each ends a shoot).

traits.perianth.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): whorls barely differentiated in Musaceae, Strelitziaceae, Heliconiaceae (tepals); the ginger group (Zingiberaceae, Costaceae, Cannaceae, Marantaceae) has calyx and corolla and holds most species, so the monocot value is wrong here.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: APweb Zingiberales page (read 2026-10-16): flowers monosymmetric (order); Cannaceae and Marantaceae asymmetric.

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): a labellum (fused staminodes) in Zingiberaceae, Costaceae and Lowiaceae, which together hold most species; banana group otherwise.

traits.ovary_position.note: APweb Zingiberales page (read 2026-10-16): ovary inferior throughout.

traits.stamens.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): one fertile stamen (or half-stamen) in Zingiberaceae, Costaceae, Cannaceae and Marantaceae; five in Musaceae, Heliconiaceae, Lowiaceae and most Strelitziaceae; six in Ravenala. Typical 1 by species weight.

traits.hypanthium.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): no floral cup described; the tube above the ovary is perianth.

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia Marantaceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers usually bisexual; APweb: bisexual flowers throughout except Musaceae (unisexual flowers on one plant).

traits.rosette.note: APweb (read 2026-10-16): leaf sheaths form pseudostems; Zingiberaceae and Costaceae leafy stems. Basal fans in Strelitzia and bananas' crowded pseudostem leaves are the minority.
